transport: Active analogue millivolt output, no protocol. Wired into Sensor Card/Box analog input (8), the voltage-signal input. Three ranges selected in Fronius Solar.Service: 0-100 mV, 0-200 mV, 0-1000 mV. Channel accuracy 3% of reading. Reachable only through the Sensor Box/Card and thence the Datamanager Solar API.
gotchas: THE CALIBRATION FACTOR IS PER-UNIT AND PRINTED ON THE SENSOR. Quick Guide, verbatim: 'It is necessary to enter the calibration factor. The calibration factor for the Fronius Insolation Sensor is at the label on the insolation sensor.' There is no fleet-wide constant. A driver cannot compute W/m2 from anything it knows;

DO NOT USE 70 mV = 1000 W/m2. DATCOM Detail contains that figure, but as an illustration - 'The conversion factor depends on the irradiance sensor and is specified in the sensor datasheet (e.g., 70 mV corresponds to 1000 W/ m2)'. It is an example value, not the Fronius sensor's sensitivity. Hardcoding it would be exact

Channel accuracy is 3% of reading, before whatever the probe's own uncertainty is. The probe's own accuracy, spectral response, temperature coefficient and tilt/soiling behaviour are NOT recorded - no per-product datasheet was found. MISSING EVIDENCE: a Fronius datasheet for the irradiance sensor product.
The measuring range (0-100 / 0-200 / 0-1000 mV) is a Solar.Service setting, not autoranging. Wrong range selected means clipping or a tenth of the resolution, with no error reported.
Sensor cable must not exceed 30 m 'so that measurement results are not distorted' (vendor).
unmappedReports: Cumulative irradiation energy (Wh/m2, kWh/m2). Not produced by this probe on its own channel - channel 2 is instantaneous W/m2 - but it is in the Solar.Service unit list and appears in the vendor's own NowSensorData example, so a site may well be logging insolation energy. No MetricKind and no Unit for energy per area.
